teaching.hint: What does multiplying ratios along a chain of shared variables do?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: An equation and its reciprocal are weighted connections; multiplying weights along a path telescopes intermediate variables.
solution_outline.approach: Build a bidirectional weighted relation graph. For each query, reject undefined endpoints; otherwise search from numerator to denominator, multiplying weights along a found path.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The running path product is the ratio from the query numerator to the current node; visited nodes prevent cycles.
solution_outline.correctness: Each edge represents a true ratio, so path multiplication yields the endpoint ratio. Consistency makes any found path valid; disconnected or undefined endpoints cannot be related from the equations.
solution_outline.complexity: O(E+Q(V+E)) time and O(V+E) graph space, plus O(V) search workspace, with E equations and Q queries.
solution_outline.pitfall: Returning one for an absent variable divided by itself treats an undefined symbol as known.

common_wrong_turns: Multiply ratios in the wrong direction
source_fidelity_notes: Retained unknown-self-query distinction and consistency guarantee; simplified long query examples.
